subject: Nebula Health — GPU pool sizing & reserved commit proposal
messages:
From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@nebulahealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@nebulahealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up on the cluster/load test results + sizing ask

Sergio — thanks again for coordinating last week's run. We ran a replay of peak production traffic on 2026-02-10 and attached the raw TPS trace and token distribution. Our main asks: a) an explicit sizing recommendation (GPU count + model config) to hit sustained 180 TPS at 512-token averages with 99th percentile latency < 250ms, and b) committed pricing for 12- and 24-month terms including any applicable discounts and SLAs.

Quick context:
- Model: customer-tuned 13B LLM (mixed quant)
- Observed peak: 210 TPS sustained for 6 minutes, median 140 TPS
- Typical burst pattern: short spikes up to +60% for 30–90s intervals

I've attached: nebula_tps_export_20260210.csv (raw), token_histograms.png (inline in Drive link). Can you return a short proposal by EOD Tuesday? Procurement will want a clear per-month committed price and an explanation of how failover/overage is handled.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Johnson
Director, ML Platforms | Nebula Health
[Attachment: nebula_tps_export_20260210.csv (csv)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@nebulahealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on the cluster/load test results + sizing ask

Emma — thanks for the data. We're reviewing the trace now and I looped Dev on the sizing question. High level takeaway up front: if your target is sustained 180 TPS @ 512 tokens with tight p99s, we should be looking at an 8–16 GPU reserved pool depending on model tuning and KV cache locality. The options:

- 8x A100 (shared pool with autoscale burst to 16): expected sustained ~160–220 TPS depending on batching and cache hit rates.
- 16x A100 (dedicated steady pool): more predictable p99s and easier to guarantee throughput SLOs.
- We can also offer a hybrid commit: smaller base commit + burst capacity with a known overage rate.

I'll ask Dev to drop a quick internal benchmark summary and a recommended commit recommendation (12 vs 24 mo) with example pricing tiers. I'll attach our current quote draft (redwood_dedicated_quote_v3.xlsx) and a summary PDF of internal runs.

Next steps: Dev will confirm the mapping from your replay to our internal 13B quantized profile and give a small risk note about prefix caching. If you can confirm the traffic shape for business hours vs off hours that helps fine-tune the commit.

- Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_quote_v3.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-13T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: sizing notes + quick internal benchmark summary

Sergio/Marissa — I ran the replay against our 32-GPU internal harness to build a mapping. Short summary:

- Baseline: our 13B quant profile (fp16-like mixed-int8 path) yields ~11–13 tokens/ms per A100 v4 equivalent in a continuous batching setup.
- Replay mapping: Nebula trace equates to ~150–200 concurrent requests with 512-token avg -> approx 160–210 TPS depending on cache hit rates.
- Config knobs that materially change sizing: batch window (10–25ms), prefix/KV cache retention, and model quant profile.

Practical sizing guidance:
- Conservative: 16 GPUs dedicated -> consistent headroom to hold 250 TPS sustained with p99s < 200ms in our runs.
- Cost-optimized: 8 GPUs with burst policy (autoscale to 24 for 30s bursts) -> lower commit but higher operational complexity and potential p99 variance.

Risks: long-tail spikes (>2x typical traffic) will need either pre-warming or burst capacity; KV cache misses during cold starts significantly inflate latency.

Attached: redwood_internal_32gpu_tps_summary.pdf and a simple map of 8/16/32 GPU economics (nebulah_proposed_map_8_16_32.pdf). Recommend we present these 2 options to Nebula with explicit delta on p99 and monthly committed price.

- Dev
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_internal_32gpu_tps_summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@nebulahealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@nebulahealth.com>, Nebula Health Procurement <procurement@nebulahealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: sizing notes + quick internal benchmark summary

Thanks Dev — this is helpful. Two clarifications from procurement and platform:

1) Procurement will need a clear price delta between 12- and 24-month commits and any early-termination/true-up language. Is the discount linear per year or do you tier it by commit size?
2) Platform asked whether the latency SLOs can be backed by credits (i.e., p99 > target triggers crediting) and how logs/tracing are exported for our auditors.

Budget note: we have a soft budget cap that makes the 24-month at larger commit attractive, but procurement needs explicit numbers and a pointer to the DocuSign quote. Could you produce a short one-page proposal (pricing table + sizing rationale + overage policy + SLA bullets) we can hand to our CFO / procurement this week?

Emma
[Forwarded inline: excerpt from security team asking about retention of inference traces — happy to open a separate thread if you prefer]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-02-17T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal: 16-GPU committed pool (primary) + burst fabric — pricing summary

Emma/Tom/Procurement — attaching a concise one-pager and a revised quote. Executive summary below. Full quote attached: redwood_dedicated_quote_v3.xlsx (v3: includes 12/24mo tables and SLA clauses).

Executive summary:
- Recommended baseline: 16x A100 (dedicated steady pool) sized for 250 TPS headroom given your replay shape.
- Pricing (examples):
  * 12-month commit (16 GPUs): $78,000/month (list) — offered discount 12% -> $68,640/month
  * 24-month commit (16 GPUs): $74,000/month (list) — offered discount 20% -> $59,200/month
  * Hybrid option (8 GPU commit + burst to 24): $44,500/month (12mo) with 10% discount for 24mo
- Overages: billed at an agreed overage rate per-GPU-hour; we also offer a pooled overage allowance (first 5% of usage/month) on 24mo deals.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime; latency SLO for agreed workload profile with credits (service credit % tied to p99 miss bands).
- Deliverables: DocuSign-ready quote (link below), 1-week onboarding playbook, Grafana dashboard share, and a 30-day quality watch window post-launch.

Links: DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/ENVELOPE/ZXCV12345
Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example.com/d/nbh-loadtests/nebulah-2026-02
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcDEF-ghij_kLmnop

If this looks ok I'll push the DocuSign and loop in Solutions Eng for a 30-minute kickoff to confirm runbook and access.
